body.statement:
Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie's Theorem 3.2 studies staggered DiD observed data \((Y_1,\ldots,Y_T,X,G)\) under their random-sampling, overlap, no-anticipation, and all-period parallel-trends assumptions. If \(\operatorname{IF}^{\operatorname{att}(g,t)}_{\mathrm{stg}}\) stacks their noncollinear DiD influence functions based on the available baseline periods and comparison cohorts and \(\Omega_{gt}(X)\) is its conditional second-moment matrix, their efficient influence function is the normalized conditional precision combination
\[
\operatorname{EIF}^{\operatorname{att}(g,t)}_{\mathrm{stg}}
=\frac{\mathbf 1'\Omega_{gt}(X)^{-1}}{\mathbf 1'\Omega_{gt}(X)^{-1}\mathbf 1}
\operatorname{IF}^{\operatorname{att}(g,t)}_{\mathrm{stg}}.
\]
The theorem's observed vector contains no eligibility variable and its parallel-trends restrictions are DiD restrictions, not the four-cell eligibility-gap equalities used by the present DDD model.

source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 3.2. Suppose that treatment adoption is staggered over time. Under Assumptions S, O, NA and PT-All, \(\operatorname{EIF}^{\operatorname{att}(g,t)}_{\mathrm{stg}}=\{\mathbf 1'\Omega_{gt}(X)^{-1}\}/\{\mathbf 1'\Omega_{gt}(X)^{-1}\mathbf 1\}\operatorname{IF}^{\operatorname{att}(g,t)}_{\mathrm{stg}}\) is the efficient influence function of \(\operatorname{ATT}(g,t)\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from arXiv:2506.17729, Theorem 3.2, together with the observed-data vector and stacked-influence-function definitions in Lemma 3.2 and the paragraphs immediately preceding the theorem.
